Subject: SIG follow-up: BCP / DR details and runbook request

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the SIG submission earlier this week. Our security team reviewed the BCP/DR responses and asked for a few clarifications so we can complete our vendor risk assessment. Specifically we need:

- A succinct runbook (PDF) that covers the steps to perform a regional failover for hosted inference traffic and control-plane operations (order of operations, who runs what, and estimated time per step).
- RTO and RPO targets you commit to for customer-facing inference endpoints, for both a warm-standby failover and a cold restore. Please separate values for: control plane (auth/quotas/orchestration), model artifact availability, and customer metadata.
- Backup cadence and retention for critical artifacts (model artifacts, metadata DB, audit logs), including cross-region replication and KMS details.
- Testing cadence (how often you rehearse failover) and most recent test dates (summary is fine).

Can you provide the runbook and a one-page summary of the RTO/RPO commitments by end of next week (we're aiming to finish vendor review by 8/20)? If some items require procurement/contract language (SLA commitment), flag them and we'll route to our procurement team.

Appreciate it — Sophie
Sophie Turner

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our BCP runbook (redwood_bcp_runbook_v3.pdf) and a short RTO/RPO summary (rto_rpo_summary.xlsx). Key items up-front: 

- High-level commitments (customer-facing):
  • Control plane orchestration: warm-standby failover target RTO = 1 hour (failover initiation to control-plane resume for critical routes).
  • Inference path (stateless serving nodes + KV-cache warm): target RTO = 2 hours for customer traffic in warm-standby; cold restore to full capacity (reloading large model artifacts) = 8 hours.
  • RPO: for critical metadata (customer config, quota state) = <= 5 minutes (asynchronously replicated across regions); for persistent audit logs and metrics = hourly increments (RPO <= 1 hour).

- Backups & replication:
  • Model artifacts: stored in encrypted object storage with cross-region replication (primary -> secondary region). Immutable snapshots taken daily with incremental uploads; snapshot retention 30 days by default (longer retention available by contract).
  • Metadata DB: point-in-time backups every 5 minutes (continuous WAL shipping), retained according to plan (default 30 days).
  • Audit logs: aggregated into encrypted log buckets, hourly rollups, retained 90 days (default). All backups encrypted with customer-tenant KMS keys where requested.

- Tests & rehearsals:
  • Weekly smoke failovers in staging for routing and autoscaling validation.
  • Quarterly full DR rehearsals (end-to-end) for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted runs have semi-annual full rehearsals with post-mortem. Last major rehearsal: 2026-05-12 (staging) and 2026-02-10 (production smoke).

The attached runbook includes step-by-step play (roles, escalation contacts, CLI commands, and fallbacks). Rishi will follow up with a short technical addendum on replication and KMS.

If you want a contractual SLA change (e.g., guaranteed RTO <=2 hours for specific inference paths), flag that back and we can route to procurement + legal for a tabletop SLA amendment.

Proposed next step: we can run a 2-hour canary failover window with your engineering team during the week of 8/23. Does that work?

Best,

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: BCP / DR details and runbook request — technical addendum

Hi Sophie — quick technical add-on to Ben's summary: 

- Replication & encryption:
  • All persistent artifacts (model blobs, DB snapshots) live in customer/tenant-scoped buckets with S3-style CRR (cross-region replication). Objects are SSE-KMS encrypted; customer-managed keys (CMKs) supported via KMS integrations.
  • Snapshots are immutable and versioned. We maintain a cryptographic checksum per snapshot and rotate snapshot storage keys quarterly.

- RPO mechanics:
  • Metadata store uses logical replication + WAL shipping; typical effective RPO under replication lag is <5 minutes under normal load. In extreme cases we fallback to last consistent snapshot (hourly).

- Failover mechanics (short):
  1) Promote secondary region control-plane endpoints (DNS TTL = 60s) and fail traffic to warm-standby GPU pools.
  2) Mount replicated model artifacts from secondary S3 buckets (incremental sync allowed); if artifacts are large and need cold pull, we start a prioritized artifact prefetch based on active customer routes.
  3) Rehydrate customer KV caches; transient cache misses are expected during first 20–30 minutes.

- Test cadence & evidence: we keep runbook outputs and test logs in the DR audit folder (Drive link included in Ben's email). We can provide the last three full rehearsal runbooks and the post-mortem notes as evidence bundles.

Happy to schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough with your infra team this week if helpful.

– Rishi Malhotra
Head of Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
